title: Starglen payments edge integration scratchpad
body:
Meeting notes (2024-10-08) — initial scoping call with Starglen Payments (Amy Park - Head of Platform, Jordan Li - Infra)

- Attendees: Amy Park (Starglen), Jordan Li (Starglen), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood infra), Maya Alvarez (Redwood SRE)

Primary ask
- Starglen wants a low-latency fraud-review assistant that runs at POS terminals in their high-volume kiosk stores. Must be able to do short text reranking + categorical tagging of suspicious transactions with < 90ms p95 latency at the terminal.
- Data classification: only transaction metadata + merchant-provided descriptors. No card PANs should leave the terminal (PCI concern).

High-level architecture discussed
- On-device model (quantized L2) for primary inference path inside store network (edge box), fallback to Redwood Hosted API in region for rare/complex cases.
- Control plane in Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) for model/version pinning and rollout; telemetry and traces shipped via customer s3/kinesis.

Key constraints / gotchas called out by customer
- PCI / tokenization: Starglen will insist on tokenized payloads from their POS. They will only send token IDs and merchant metadata to any external service. We must ensure our hosted fallback never receives PANs and that on-device changes are auditable.
- Offline stores: ~7% of stores are occasionally offline (cellular fallback). Edge box must queue inference requests locally and re-sync logs; they want local decisioning to avoid blocking checkout.
- Memory cap on edge box: 8GB RAM usable for model and runtime — need to validate quantized model footprints and a smaller KV-cache strategy.
- Cold-start jitter: terminals spawn many short lived processes; runtime must avoid repeated model load thrash. Suggest long-lived inference daemon + warmup hooks.
- Throughput pattern: bursty at checkout peaks (every 1–2 minutes) but overall low sustained qps. Batching needs to be adaptive and preserve latencies for single-checkout flows.

Technical questions we need to answer (actionable items)
1) Model size options + quantization profiles that fit 8GB RAM with KV cache active. (Owner: Ravi) — deliver sample footprints and estimated p95 memory.
2) Strategy for tokenization / PAN redaction: will Starglen provide token mapping service in-store or via Redwood Private? (Owner: Avery) — confirm during next call with Amy.
3) Fallback SLAs: what model family can be used in Hosted fallback that gives compatible outputs? Need deterministic fallback mapping rules for label alignment. (Owner: Maya)
4) Telemetry pipeline and retention: maps to their compliance table; need example data flows and examples of logs that exclude PANs. (Owner: Samir)
5) Warmup and process lifecycle guidance for their POS daemon (Owner: Ravi)

Immediate engineering gotchas we noted
- Quantized model inference on ARM64 CPU in the edge boxes has non-linear latency pattern when sequence length > 64. Need to instrument synthetic workloads that mimic transaction descriptions (avg token length ~ 24 tokens).
- KV cache persistence across reboots: they expect quick resumption. We'll propose periodic checkpointing to local disk with encryption-at-rest via customer KMS.
- Observability: they want request->decision trace across edge and hosted fallback. We need a lightweight trace header that survives queueing and offline resync.
- Billing/usage: They are price-sensitive; must provide unit economics for edge vs hosted fallback (tokens vs inference time). Customer wants a blended per-transaction cost estimate for 50k tx/day.

Security / compliance notes
- PCI scope reduction is critical. Avoid storing PANs anywhere in Redwood. Confirm we can sign BAA/PCI addendum and support on-prem HSM for key material if needed.
- Audit logs must be customer-controlled and immutable for 90 days.

Notes from demo ask
- Starglen asked to see a small PoC: run a quantized 7B-class reranker on a Raspberry Pi-like device connected to a POS simulator with ~2MB description payloads. They want to see p95 latency and failure scenarios (network drop to fallback).
- Amy wants a 2-week PoC timeline with a 1-hour onsite (remote) demo mid-PoC.

Next steps (short term)
- Ravi: produce quantization+memory report and suggested model variants by 2024-10-15.
- Avery: follow up on tokenization mapping approach and push for architecture diagram from Starglen (2024-10-11).
- Maya: draft fallback mapping rules and latency SLOs to propose (2024-10-18).
- Samir: write telemetry flow draft (logs + traces + retention) and share compliance checklist (2024-10-14).
- Schedule follow-up with Amy and Jordan for 2024-10-16 (aim: finalize PoC acceptance criteria).

Loose ideas / options to explore
- Tiny distillation of our reranker into a 1–2 layer dense adapter that runs faster on ARM with similar label alignment, rather than full quantized transformer.
- Prefix-caching: maintain a short ngram prefix cache keyed by merchant id to short-circuit the model for very common descriptors.
- Local policy ruleset (customer-managed JS) to handle obvious fraud patterns and reduce reliance on model for deterministic cases.

Informal reminders to self
- Don’t over-sell fallbacks as feature parity — we need to clearly document where hosted fallback will differ.
- Keep pricing scenarios simple: per-transaction edge cost + hosted fallback per-token cost + monthly infra fee.

Rough checklist for PoC deliverables
- Minimal Docker + systemd package for edge daemon (auto-update disabled by default).
- Quantized model artifact (sizes + hash), sample inference harness, and synthetic workload runner.
- Short README for their infra team on how to provide tokenized payloads and keys.
- Predefined test cases that cover: normal tx, suspicious tx (true positive), suspicious tx (false positive), network drop during request.

Open risks
- If quantized model cannot meet 90ms p95 on their hardware, they may insist on specialized edge hardware or revert to hosted-only which breaks their offline requirement.
- Legal timeline for PCI addendum could delay PoC start.

Bottom line: PoC looks feasible but hinges on model footprint and tokenization architecture. Next call: confirm tokenization flow and get an infra diagram from Starglen.
